review_scope: Author-level delta and receiving-use consistency check of the depth lemma against its main-manuscript resource-capacity invocation; not an independent audit of the full new tilted-transfer theorem.
findings: The actual physical encoder C_n lies inside the expurgated QA. The bound F_Q <= 2 r_A^2 epsilon I is a joint operator bound and hence uniform over logical inputs and arbitrary references.

The initial tau_pi split is positive and depth diagonal. Its tail is charged analytically, with mass 3^(-(A+1)) and mean contribution (A+3/2)3^(-(A+1)); no physical truncation or postselection is introduced.

Finite propagation converts uniform overflow into the stated first-moment bound. Its two correction terms vanish, giving H_n+o(1)=O_beta(log n), and O_beta(log N) because k is fixed before n tends to infinity.

The main definition imposes final mean depth o(N) explicitly as an additional resource condition at tau_pi on the encoded maximally mixed input. The lower code satisfies the stronger uniform-logical-input O(log N) condition.

The all-normal pointwise full-diamond reliability quantifier is retained separately from the mean-depth guarantee at tau_pi. The normal infinite-mean initializer counterexample prevents extending the resource guarantee to all normal states.

All forward calls count. Padding by fewer than k calls preserves rate, logical reliability and sublinear depth cost. No terminal bath-return condition, fresh bath or auxiliary-normalization implementation is added.

Conditional on the separately reviewed all-input entropy-drift upper and reliable-code entropy lemma, the stated resource-capacity upper pairs correctly with the actual inherited lower code to give excess Theta(beta^2), without making an unrestricted-capacity claim.
